window-1.title: Every Place at Once
window-1.blurb: It's the Every Noise map rebuilt as cities instead of genres — click Singapore and find out which places on earth are listening like you are, then fall down a rabbit hole into someone else's hometown radio.

window-2.title: Dirt
window-2.blurb: It's the culture newsletter that treats a Ghibli frame, a dead website and a pop star's tour merch with equal seriousness — exactly your brain, but in essay form.

window-3.title: Chrysanthemum Osmanthus Citrus Sparkler
window-3.blurb: It's your grandma's dried-flower tea jar turned into a golden, fizzy spritz — heritage flavors you already know by heart, dressed up enough to photograph.

window-4.title: A Clinton Hill Brownstone with Chinese Inflections by Bespoke Only
window-4.blurb: It's 19th-century Shanghai smuggled into a Brooklyn brownstone — proof you can build heritage into a room as texture and mood instead of hanging it on the wall like a souvenir.

window-5.title: Inner Teahouse, Chinatown
window-5.blurb: A second-floor shophouse teahouse born out of a pottery studio, where the cups are as considered as the tea — exactly the kind of quiet, hand-made hideout you'd claim as your own and accidentally leave with a new side quest.
